hazards.mechanism: One payment_status conflates commercial intent, attempt, authorization, capture, settlement, refund, dispute, and fulfillment.
hazards.evidence: List every entity, cardinality, amount dimension, evidence source, and independent lifecycle hidden behind the field.
hazards.control: Model separate entities and derive customer-facing summaries from them instead of making the summary authoritative.
hazards.detection: Find transitions that mean different things by rail or overwrite another lifecycle dimension.
hazards.recovery: Reconstruct child entities from provider and ledger evidence, then migrate reads before writes.
hazards.test: Represent captured-but-not-settled, partially-refunded-and-disputed, and fulfilled-but-reversed without contradictory status.

hazards.mechanism: Two payment attempts for one order both succeed after a timeout, failover, or customer retry.
hazards.evidence: Inspect intent-to-attempt cardinality, winning-attempt rule, provider object IDs, idempotency keys, and late-success handling.
hazards.control: Allow many attempts but enforce one intended payable amount, block new attempts while one is indeterminate, and classify late extra success.
hazards.detection: Alert when successful captured totals across attempts exceed the commercial intent.
hazards.recovery: Stop fulfillment duplication, select the intended payment, and refund/reverse the extra success idempotently.
hazards.test: Let attempt B succeed after A timed out, then deliver a late success for A.

hazards.mechanism: Every transition is legal, but concurrent partial captures, refunds, or disputes make cumulative amounts exceed their parents.
hazards.evidence: Define intended, authorized, capturable, captured, refundable, refunded, disputed, and settled amounts per asset.
hazards.control: Guard state and cumulative amount invariants atomically under optimistic versioning or locks.
hazards.detection: Continuously verify amount conservation and remaining-capacity equations.
hazards.recovery: Freeze further modifications, identify the racing operations, and reverse unintended excess movement.
hazards.test: Race partial captures and refunds whose individual amounts are valid but combined total is not.

hazards.mechanism: A provider confirms success after the local intent was canceled, expired, or declared failed following an ambiguous response.
hazards.evidence: Distinguish local policy cancellation from authoritative provider cancellation and preserve the pending attempt identity.
hazards.control: Keep ambiguous attempts recoverable and define a late-success compensation transition rather than rejecting the fact.
hazards.detection: Alert on success facts for locally terminal intents or losing attempts.
hazards.recovery: Record the success, block duplicate fulfillment, and execute the approved refund, void, or manual-review policy.
hazards.test: Cancel locally after timeout, then receive capture confirmation and settlement.

hazards.mechanism: An older failure or cancellation fact overwrites a newer capture because transitions use arrival time or last-write-wins.
hazards.evidence: Record source version/sequence, effective time, observed time, prior state, and strength of evidence.
hazards.control: Use guarded transitions and an explicit evidence precedence policy; route contradictions to reconciliation.
hazards.detection: Count stale and illegal transitions by mapping version and source.
hazards.recovery: Restore the state supported by stronger evidence while preserving the stale fact and incident trail.
hazards.test: Deliver stale failure after captured and with the same timestamp but lower provider version.

hazards.mechanism: A partial capture is incorrectly marked final, or concurrent captures consume more than the remaining authorized amount.
hazards.evidence: Inspect final_capture semantics, multicapture eligibility, remaining capturable amount, authorization expiry, and capture idempotency.
hazards.control: Make capture a child operation with atomic remaining-amount guards and explicit finality.
hazards.detection: Alert on captures after finalization, expiry, or cumulative cap exhaustion.
hazards.recovery: Do not invent another capture; reconcile provider result and adjust fulfillment or refund excess.
hazards.test: Race two final partial captures and attempt a later shipment capture.

hazards.mechanism: Reauthorization creates a new authorization ID, but captures continue against the expired original or history is overwritten.
hazards.evidence: Model authorization lineage, honor/expiry windows, replacement ID, amount, and captures bound to each authorization.
hazards.control: Create a new authorization entity linked to the prior one and route future captures to the active identity.
hazards.detection: Alert on capture commands targeting superseded or expired authorization IDs.
hazards.recovery: Resolve the active provider authorization before retrying and preserve both authorization records.
hazards.test: Reauthorize near expiry and verify capture uses the replacement ID and shortened remaining window.

hazards.mechanism: An incremental authorization increases the amount and code assumes it also extended the original expiry.
hazards.evidence: Track amount changes and expiry as independent fields sourced from the provider after every increment.
hazards.control: Refresh capturable amount and capture-before deadline separately; schedule capture from the actual deadline.
hazards.detection: Alert when fulfillment or capture scheduling exceeds the current authorization expiry.
hazards.recovery: Reauthorize where supported or cancel/adjust fulfillment before attempting an expired capture.
hazards.test: Approve an increment without changing expiry and advance time past the original deadline.

hazards.mechanism: A refund remains pending while a dispute reimburses the customer, producing duplicate customer compensation and ledger exposure.
hazards.evidence: Correlate charge, refund status, dispute lifecycle, provider balance entries, and customer communication.
hazards.control: Make refunds and disputes separate entities with a cross-process compensation policy for the same captured amount.
hazards.detection: Alert when pending refund plus open/won dispute coverage exceeds captured exposure.
hazards.recovery: Follow provider-specific cancellation/acceptance policy, stop duplicate manual payout, and reconcile returned funds.
hazards.test: Open a dispute while a refund is pending, then exercise both refund-failed and refund-succeeded outcomes.

hazards.mechanism: The system tells the customer a refund is complete, but the provider later marks it failed and returns funds to the platform balance.
hazards.evidence: Define refund requested, pending, succeeded, failed, canceled, and returned-funds evidence plus notification timing.
hazards.control: Communicate status precisely, listen for refund updates/failure, and keep alternative-remediation ownership.
hazards.detection: Monitor aged pending refunds, failed refunds, and customer messages inconsistent with current state.
hazards.recovery: Notify operations/customer, arrange an approved alternative refund, and post the provider-returned balance movement.
hazards.test: Move a refund from pending to failed after an initial acknowledgement and verify notification and ledger correction.
